title: SharpCell.Grid
summary: A free (MIT) Excel-like spreadsheet control for .NET 8 and later, built on the SharpCell formula engine: it shows a worksheet the way Excel does, with number formats, cell styles, column widths, row heights, merged cells, frozen panes and text running on over empty cells. Only the visible cells are read, so any sheet size scrolls smoothly.
details: Packages: `SharpCell.Grid` (geometry, hit testing and painting, no UI framework), `SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia` (`SpreadsheetView`, the Avalonia control) and `SharpCell.Grid.Wpf` (`SpreadsheetView` for WPF, Windows only). Namespaces: `SharpCell.Grid`, `SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia`, `SharpCell.Grid.Wpf`; workbooks come from `SharpCell` and `SharpCell.Xlsx`. The view reads cells when it paints: after changing cells or recalculating, call `InvalidateVisual()`; after changing sizes or frozen panes, call `ReloadLayout()`. Cells are selected, copied and edited as in Excel (`Selection`, `CopyAsync()`, `BeginEdit()`, `Editor`, `Edited`, `IsReadOnly`, `FormulaBar`; without a UI framework `GridSelection`, `GridClipboard`, `GridEditor`); what is typed is read by SharpCell's `Cell.Input`.
